routes.description: Establish robust non-naturalist normative realism by treating objective normative facts as legitimate explananda, defending normative appearances as justified starting points, and showing that realism best preserves ordinary judgment, deliberation, and language under holistic comparison.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if objective normative facts remain warranted components of inquiry, challenges from intuition diversity and causal genealogy do not defeat that warrant, and rival pragmatist or attitude-based accounts fail to explain the relevant normative phenomena without comparable commitments.

motionBridge.description: Connect justified mind-independent normative facts, including moral facts, to the motion's claim that objective moral truths exist and favor realism over global normative anti-realism.

centralBridges.description: Show why normative facts themselves, rather than only beliefs, behavior, or linguistic practices, are legitimate phenomena requiring explanation.
Explain why plausible normative appearances can justify inquiry without prior proof and why unshared intuitions do not establish epistemic parity.
Demonstrate through holistic comparison that realism preserves normative judgment and deliberation with lower theoretical costs than its rivals.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish genuine causal debunking evidence from cultural variation, minority status, disagreement, or the mere absence of explicit folk metaethical views.
Require attitude-based semantics and quietism to account for counterfactual moral claims, ordinary linguistic practice, and the apparent intelligibility of metaethical questions.

routes.description: Establish global normative anti-realism by denying realism any privileged intuitive or explanatory starting point and providing pragmatist, psychological, and meaning-in-use accounts of moral judgment, language, deliberation, and opposition without objective non-naturalist facts.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if realist appearances can be explained without truth-tracking access, ordinary moral practice carries no necessary realist commitment, and objective normative facts add no explanatory work beyond a more parsimonious descriptive account.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of a warranted or explanatorily necessary objective normative posit to global normative anti-realism and rejection of objective moral truths.

centralBridges.description: Show that realist intuitions and normative appearances are neither universal nor entitled to methodological priority over anti-realist starting points.
Explain moral psychology, deliberation, behavior, and discourse through attitudes, communicative intentions, social practices, and empirical causal accounts.
Establish that realism supplies no indispensable explanation and that a pragmatist framework can dissolve or bypass its proposed metaphysical problem.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify an error-producing causal history or methodological mechanism capable of explaining localized realist belief without tracking objective normative truth.
Account for sincere condemnation, counterfactual opposition, and action-guiding moral speech without committing speakers or sentences to mind-independent moral facts.

sections.title: Scope, Explananda, and Comparative Burdens
sections.rationale: The debate first turns on whether the target is morality or normativity generally, whether normative facts themselves belong among the data, and how competing theoretical packages should be compared.

sections.title: Normative Appearances and Epistemic Priority
sections.rationale: The central epistemic clash concerns whether realist appearances may function as justified starting points, whether contrary intuitions create parity, and whether disagreement without persuasion affects warrant.

sections.title: Moral Judgment, Language, and Deliberation
sections.rationale: Both routes must explain objective-seeming judgments, counterfactual wrongness, sincere condemnation, linguistic meaning, and action-guiding deliberation while establishing whether those practices carry realist commitments.

sections.title: Empirical Genealogy, Variation, and Debunking
sections.rationale: Cultural variation, folk research, minority status, shared philosophical methods, and causal error hypotheses matter insofar as they distinguish harmless diversity from a genuine debunking explanation.

sections.title: Explanatory Necessity, Parsimony, and Quietism
sections.rationale: The culminating comparative issue is whether objective normative facts perform indispensable explanatory work or whether pragmatist and descriptive accounts explain moral practice more parsimoniously and challenge the framing itself.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: Robust non-naturalist realism vindicates ordinary normative judgment and deliberation by treating objective normative truths as discovered, mind-independent, nonconventional, abstract facts.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly gives David the floor, and the uninterrupted opening statement presents the position in the first person.

response.rationale: Constructive statement defining robust realism and connecting its mind-independent truths to ordinary normative judgment and deliberation.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly establishes the position and its intended vindicatory role, though it does not yet defend the posit.

precisionFindings.rationale: The passage explicitly identifies non-naturalist realism, objectivity, mind-independence, and discovery; its intended scope and commitments are recoverable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The constitutive description is appropriately firm, but the broader claim of vindicating judgment is announced more confidently than the excerpt independently warrants.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The definition and vindication claim cohere, with one implicit bridge from preserving ordinary appearances to favoring the ontology.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The excerpt supplies a clear account of the view but compresses the material warrant that objective abstract facts actually explain deliberation.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the motion bridge by asserting objective normative truths and linking them to realism's treatment of judgment.

representationalCharity.rationale: This constructive definition does not engage a sufficiently developed competing interpretation to make a charity test meaningful.

moves.evidenceBasis: The selected excerpt expressly describes objective truths as independent of us and as objects discovered through successful normative inquiry.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: The fundamental realist dispute concerns normativity as a whole rather than morality alone, because moral truths are one subset of a wider class that also includes epistemic and prudential normative truths.
moves.attributionBasis: This remains within David's uninterrupted opening statement and is framed as his own clarification of the realist position.

response.rationale: Constructive clarification expands the explanandum from morality alone to the wider category of normative facts, including epistemic cases.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, the scope claim is explicit and supported by a concrete nonmoral normative example.

precisionFindings.rationale: The morality/normativity relation is stated directly and the epistemic example fixes the intended broader scope without material instability.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The taxonomic claim is proportionate to the example and includes the qualification that some normative truths are not easily classified as moral.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The subset relation and the example of epistemic justification provide an explicit, consistent inference to broader normative scope.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: A representative epistemic example supports the distinction, though the move does not independently establish that all such facts are objective.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It centrally identifies normative facts as the relevant data, while the final defense of their reality remains for later argument.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move clarifies scope rather than characterizing or rejecting a developed opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt states that morality is a subset of normativity and illustrates the wider category with norms against wishful belief formation.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: A defense of realism must answer epistemic, semantic, motivational, and disagreement objections while comparing realism's preservation of normative phenomena with the available rival theories.
moves.attributionBasis: The uninterrupted first-person methodological discussion continues under David's expressly assigned opening-statement turn.

response.rationale: Constructive methodological move specifies that realism must preserve the phenomena, answer major objections, and compare available alternatives.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly formulates a demanding comparative procedure rather than merely asserting realism's conclusion.

precisionFindings.rationale: The project, objections, relevant phenomena, and rival comparison are expressly identified, with no evaluation-obscuring scope shift.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim concerns what a satisfactory defense must do, and the enumerated objections and comparative check fit that methodological necessity.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The proposed method consistently links saving the phenomena, addressing objections, and examining rival explanations.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The methodological warrant is plausible and specifically structured, though no actual comparison is completed in this span.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supplies the central comparative-vindication standard but does not itself demonstrate that realism satisfies it.

representationalCharity.rationale: No particular rival theory is represented in enough detail here to test charitable treatment.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt expressly requires answering objections and checking whether alternative views can save the same normative phenomena.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: Metaethical theories should be assessed holistically by their cumulative plausibility, and realism preserves substantial normative phenomena at a lower theoretical cost than competing packages.
moves.attributionBasis: David explicitly describes his preferred philosophical method and contrasts realism's overall package with competing views, including Lance's.

response.rationale: Constructive move advances holistic package comparison and claims realism retains desired phenomena at lower cost than opponents suppose.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, the comparative framework is clear, but the favorable cost assessment remains compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The holistic comparison is recoverable, but 'plausibility points,' what one wants, and theoretical price remain only partly specified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Comparative language appropriately recognizes package-level judgment, but the claim that realism's price is lower lacks an explicit cost inventory.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Holistic comparison is coherent, but the bridge from preserving desired phenomena to a lower overall theoretical price is materially compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The passage asserts favorable comparative costs without representative rival analysis or a defended weighting of benefits and liabilities.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly addresses the indispensable comparative-vindication bridge and proposes the metric by which the packages should be assessed.

representationalCharity.rationale: Rival packages are mentioned abstractly and no sufficiently specific alternative is characterized for a meaningful charity test.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says realism supplies much of what is wanted at lower cost and expressly calls final evaluation comparative and holistic.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: Historical, evolutionary, and cultural variation in moral beliefs and practices does not by itself undermine mind-independent moral facts, because the contingent genealogy of belief must be distinguished from the facts believed.
moves.attributionBasis: David introduces the passage as a preemptive clarification and consistently distinguishes realist claims from claims about social practice and belief.

response.rationale: Constructive move distinguishes timeless mind-independent facts from the historically contingent social practice and genealogy of moral belief.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it states a clear distinction that directly constrains what genealogical evidence can establish.

precisionFindings.rationale: Facts, practices, histories, evolutionary explanations, and cultural variation are expressly distinguished without conflating their scopes.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move does not deny historical or evolutionary variation; it makes the bounded claim that such variation alone does not settle fact-dependence.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction validly blocks an immediate inference from contingent belief formation to contingency or absence of the believed facts.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual distinction is well supported by explicit concessions, though it does not answer a genealogy that independently shows unreliability.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It strongly supports the subsidiary debunking-limits bridge by identifying what cultural and evolutionary evidence cannot establish alone.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move anticipates a generic genealogy objection but does not portray a particular developed opponent argument.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt simultaneously affirms invariant realist facts and concedes that moralizing practices have histories, evolutionary explanations, and wide variation.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: The central dispute concerns global normative anti-realism versus non-naturalist normative realism, rather than merely the boundary between moral and nonmoral norms.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly passes the floor to Lance, who addresses David by name and identifies his own global normative anti-realist position.

components.text: Whether expanding the subject from morality to normativity removes or materially changes the parties' fundamental disagreement.
Whether objective moral truths remain directly denied under the anti-realist position.

response.rationale: Bush accepts the broader scope and expressly states that his global anti-realism denies normative realism as a whole, preserving direct opposition while reducing the importance of the moral/nonmoral boundary.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly contacts the scope clarification and states its consequence for the continuing dispute.

precisionFindings.rationale: Global normative anti-realism and its relation to moral anti-realism are expressly defined, with stable scope throughout.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move reports Bush's own position and the logical persistence of disagreement, both directly supported by the stated global denial.

charity.alternative: Enoch's scope clarification may be substantive because moral realism is embedded within a larger normative ontology.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush grants the wider ontology is the target and says only that delineating moral from nonmoral norms is not central to their disagreement.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Global denial of normative realism consistently entails denial of its moral subset and explains why the scope clarification does not dissolve disagreement.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conclusion follows directly from the explicitly defined position, with only limited external evidentiary demand.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The reply attacks the pro motion bridge by expressly denying objective normativity, including its moral subset.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response accurately preserves Enoch's broader scope while explaining why Bush's global denial keeps the dispute intact.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt explicitly defines Bush as a global normative anti-realist and states that disagreement remains despite the broader scope.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: Realism has no automatic cumulative advantage when anti-realists dispute alleged costs such as abandoning ordinary discourse or shared intuitions instead of conceding those costs.
moves.attributionBasis: Lance directly adopts David's plausibility-points framework before explaining in the first person where his assessment of benefits and costs diverges.

components.text: Whether realism's alleged preservation benefits and rival costs actually give realism a favorable holistic balance.
Whether rival theories must concede costs such as abandoning ordinary discourse or shared intuitions.

response.rationale: Bush accepts comparative package assessment but disputes the inputs, explaining that he does not concede costs which other anti-realists accept; the reply contacts the comparison without completing a rival cost accounting.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive comparative premise but only partially substantiates which alleged costs disappear and why.

precisionFindings.rationale: The disputed costs and examples are recoverable, although the metric for assessing package costs remains partly unspecified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Bush makes a bounded challenge to automatic realist advantage, grounding it in his refusal to concede specified costs rather than claiming a completed comparison.

charity.alternative: The realist comparison can count genuine explanatory losses even when an anti-realist declines to describe them as costs.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush identifies contested examples but does not show that the relevant linguistic or intuitive phenomena are preserved without loss.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Disputing the cost assignments coherently blocks an automatic cumulative advantage, but refusal to concede a cost is not itself proof that no cost exists.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Concrete examples are supplied, yet the move gives little linguistic or psychological support for treating those alleged sacrifices as costless.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the central comparative-vindication bridge by contesting the cost ledger used in holistic assessment.

representationalCharity.rationale: The realist method is represented fairly, though the response leaves its strongest explanatory-cost interpretation underanswered.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt identifies ordinary moral discourse and shared intuitions as alleged anti-realist costs that Bush declines to concede.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: Realist intuitions are neither universal nor an established default, and ordinary normative discourse and deliberation need not encode a substantive implicit metaethical commitment.
moves.attributionBasis: Lance discusses his own phenomenology and research, then repeatedly states his empirical conclusions about ordinary speakers and normative practices.

components.text: Whether ordinary normative judgment and deliberation carry the realist commitments claimed as phenomena needing vindication.
Whether preserving ordinary discourse gives realism a comparative explanatory advantage.

response.rationale: Bush directly denies that ordinary discourse is best explained by implicit realism and carefully adds that ordinary people need not instead be implicit anti-realists; this contacts the claimed realist starting phenomenon.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The decisive attribution of implicit realist commitment is expressly denied and replaced with a neutral metaethical reading of ordinary practice.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim carefully distinguishes absence of realist commitment from positive anti-realist commitment and limits itself to ordinary discourse.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The qualified conclusion is appropriate, but the excerpt alludes to research without presenting representative findings sufficient for the empirical generalization.

charity.alternative: Realism may claim only that ordinary judgments have objective-seeming content, not that speakers possess an explicit metaethical theory.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush addresses implicit commitment as well as explicit philosophical belief, but the excerpt does not fully separate semantic content from speaker belief.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The neutral reading coherently rebuts an inference from ordinary practice to either metaethical side, with a minor unresolved semantics-belief distinction.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The position is empirically framed and qualified, but the selected evidence provides conclusions rather than the underlying research design or findings.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It centrally supports the no-default-realism bridge by denying methodological priority from ordinary discourse and deliberation.

representationalCharity.rationale: The stronger implicit-commitment interpretation is substantially addressed, with a bounded omission concerning content versus belief.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says ordinary moral discourse requires neither implicit realist nor implicit anti-realist commitment and expressly qualifies both attributions.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: Realist normative appearances are not privileged merely because they seem intuitive, since anti-realist starting assumptions face the same question-begging objection and further considerations are needed.
moves.attributionBasis: A clear speaker change introduces a first-person objection to Enoch's immediately preceding claims about intuitive normative facts.

components.text: Whether realist appearances are independently entitled to priority over an anti-realist interpretation of the same normative experience.
Whether further comparative considerations are required to choose between opposed starting assumptions.

response.rationale: The hallucination and colorblindness analogy directly challenges privilege for realist intuitions and demands further considerations, contacting the epistemic priority premise while not itself establishing equal ultimate warrant.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive priority question but offers a symmetry challenge rather than a completed comparative resolution.

precisionFindings.rationale: The demand for further considerations is clear, though movement between perceptual analogy, assumptions, and normative intuitions leaves one material scope bridge.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The hallucination claim is posed as an epistemic possibility and supports only the bounded conclusion that intuition alone does not resolve the dispute.

charity.alternative: Enoch may invoke intuitive plausibility as defeasible initial justification rather than conclusive proof or dialectically neutral evidence.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush shows that opposed intuitions create a need for further comparison, but does not show that defeasible initial justification is absent.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The symmetry argument validly motivates further considerations, but possible hallucination alone does not establish epistemic parity or defeat prima facie warrant.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The analogy illustrates underdetermination but supplies no independent evidence that the realist appearance arises from an unreliable mechanism.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the central no-default-realism bridge by challenging privileged realist starting assumptions.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection is fair to the nonconclusive role of intuition but leaves the strongest modest foundationalist version partly intact.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt uses hallucination and colorblindness possibilities to argue that opposed starting assumptions require appeal to further considerations.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: Failure to persuade someone who rejects a highly plausible normative starting point does not undermine that starting point's justification or place opposed starting points on an epistemic par.
moves.attributionBasis: The response uses Enoch's characteristic realist examples and directly answers Bush's demand for a basis to privilege one intuition over another.

components.text: Whether inability to compel an opponent from shared premises removes justification from a highly plausible normative starting point.
Whether unshared ordinary intuitions establish that realism lacks any justified epistemic priority.

response.rationale: Enoch distinguishes dialectical persuasion from epistemic justification through the radical-skeptic comparison, directly answering the symmetry demand but leaving criteria for ranking the opposed starting points partly implicit.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive challenge and blocks one inference, but does not fully supply the requested independent basis for comparative privilege.

precisionFindings.rationale: Persuasion, premises, justification, radical skepticism, and parity are consistently separated, and the conclusion is expressly bounded.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The passage says failure of argument need not threaten justification and uses tentative language when applying the analogy to the present case.

charity.alternative: Bush's challenge requests reasons to rank opposed appearances, not merely an argument capable of forcing assent from a skeptic.
charity.decisiveQualification: Enoch successfully separates nonpersuasion from defeat, but does not fully provide comparative criteria for the competing starting points.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between justification and universal persuadability is sound, with one remaining bridge from highly plausible premises to superior warrant here.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The radical-skeptic analogy supports the conceptual distinction, but its applicability depends on the disputed plausibility of the realist premise.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the central epistemic-starting-points bridge by arguing that unshared intuitions do not automatically defeat justification.

representationalCharity.rationale: The strongest demand is recognized in substance, though the reply answers its skeptical implication more fully than its ranking component.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt states that inability to force a radical skeptic to accept one's premises does not by itself undermine their justification.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: Inquiry necessarily begins from what appears most plausible, and the inability to argue an opponent out of rejecting such a starting point does not itself threaten the position founded upon it.
moves.attributionBasis: The passage directly answers Bush's request for an argument and addresses the audience using Enoch's example of race-based humiliation.

components.text: What method remains available when opposed parties begin from incompatible intuitive assumptions and cannot compel agreement.
Whether a contested realist appearance may still function as an inquiry-guiding starting point.

response.rationale: Enoch answers with a plausibility-led method and acknowledges possible epistemic impasse; this addresses how inquiry starts but does not independently validate the audience's plausibility ranking.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the methodological demand and states a replacement decision procedure, while leaving the procedure's neutrality and reliability underdefended.

precisionFindings.rationale: The proposal to begin from comparative plausibility and the possibility of epistemic impasse are both explicit and stably scoped.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Some reliance on apparent plausibility is plausibly necessary, but the suggestion that inability to argue further does not threaten the position needs a reliability qualification.

charity.alternative: Bush may accept plausibility-led inquiry while denying that the realist premise is more plausible or non-question-begging.
charity.decisiveQualification: The move invites an audience comparison but does not offer a shared standard showing why the realist starting point should prevail.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The method explains how inquiry can proceed without universal premises, but it does not by itself establish that the selected plausibility ranking is truth-conducive.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The argument has intuitive methodological support and a concrete normative prompt, but no defended account of plausibility's reliability.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It centrally advances the epistemic-starting-points bridge by explaining a method for inquiry under foundational disagreement.

representationalCharity.rationale: The opposing concern is treated as possible impasse rather than caricature, though its demand for a comparative standard remains compressed.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt acknowledges possible epistemic impasse and asks the audience to compare which candidate starting point they find more plausible.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: Ordinary normative opposition should not be conflated with metaethical evidence, because anti-realism can distinguish actual from counterfactual standards and explain objective-seeming moral responses.
moves.attributionBasis: After the moderator grants Bush an uninterrupted response, Bush explicitly develops his own normative-entanglement account and its empirical debunking implications.

components.text: Whether strong first-order normative opposition establishes or privileges a realist metaethical interpretation of that opposition.
Whether the felt stability of a moral standard supplies independent support for realism.

response.rationale: Bush directly argues that first-order standards and their counterfactual stability should not be leveraged into metaethical commitment, and offers anti-realist resources for explaining steadfast opposition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It directly contacts the inference from normative commitment to realism and sketches an alternative, though the long span compresses details of that account.

precisionFindings.rationale: The first-order/metaethical distinction is clear, but 'normative entanglement' and the exact anti-realist explanatory mechanism remain partly specified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move makes a comparative explanatory claim rather than claiming logical entailment, and it distinguishes actual standards from counterfactual alternatives.

charity.alternative: The realist may treat counterfactual moral stability as evidence best explained by mind-independent truth, not as a direct entailment from opposition.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush blocks conflation and sketches accommodation, but does not fully compare the explanatory virtues of the two accounts.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Separating first-order commitment from metaethical ontology is coherent, and the actual/counterfactual standards distinction supplies a usable alternative structure.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The account offers explanatory resources but the excerpt provides limited empirical support for its broader claims about ordinary objective-seeming responses.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary moral-language-practice bridge by explaining steadfast condemnation without realist commitment.

representationalCharity.rationale: The strongest abductive interpretation is substantially preserved, although the reply focuses more sharply on rejecting a commitment attribution.

moves.evidenceBasis: The selected passage rejects attributing flexible standards to anti-realists and distinguishes normative claims from their alleged metaethical implications.

moves.speaker: David Enoch
moves.proposition: Subjectivist paraphrases fit ordinary moral language poorly, while the effort to accommodate claims that conduct would remain wrong under different attitudes concedes the realist's explanatory starting point.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker challenges Bush's proposed explanation in the second person and articulates the realist interpretation defended throughout Enoch's turns.

components.text: Whether the anti-realist accommodation of attitude-independent-sounding counterfactual wrongness fits ordinary moral language and its explanatory target.
Whether ordinary discourse gives realism any priority once counterfactual moral claims are included.

response.rationale: Enoch acknowledges that Bush offers an accommodation but argues that the need to preserve counterfactual wrongness concedes the realist's starting phenomenon; this contacts explanatory adequacy without proving uniquely realist semantics.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It directly engages the alternative accommodation and its linguistic fit, but leaves the comparative semantic argument incomplete.

precisionFindings.rationale: The counterfactual claim, linguistic-fit objection, common starting phenomenon, and disagreement over accommodation are all explicitly separated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The poor-fit claim and concession inference are plausible pressures, but the excerpt lacks enough semantic comparison to support its confident tone fully.

charity.alternative: An anti-realist can treat counterfactual wrongness as a phenomenon to explain without conceding that its content or best explanation is realist.
charity.decisiveQualification: Enoch acknowledges a different accommodation but overstates the extent to which sharing the explanandum concedes the realist starting point.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Poor fit can motivate comparison, but the inference from needing to explain a counterfactual claim to being 'with' realism equivocates between shared explanandum and ontology.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move identifies a specific linguistic datum but does not present representative usage evidence or a detailed comparison of paraphrases.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the subsidiary anti-realist moral-language bridge by pressing counterfactual wrongness and ordinary linguistic fit.

representationalCharity.rationale: The alternative is recognized rather than ignored, but its distinction between explaining a datum and accepting its realist interpretation is insufficiently preserved.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt emphasizes that wrongness under different attitudes is important to accommodate and argues that subjectivist paraphrase fits ordinary language poorly.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: Ordinary moral language supports subjectivist or anti-realist analysis at least as well as realism, so realism is not required to explain the relevant linguistic practices.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker explicitly rejects Enoch's linguistic claims, cites subjectivist linguistic work, and restates Bush's anti-realist explanatory position.

components.text: Whether ordinary moral usage and counterfactual claims linguistically favor realism over subjectivist or anti-realist analyses.
Whether ordinary moral language requires mind-independent normative truth for adequate explanation.

response.rationale: Bush expressly denies any linguistic priority for realism and invokes subjectivist linguistic analysis, directly contacting Enoch's fit claim, though the selected span mostly states rather than demonstrates the competing analysis.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The decisive linguistic-priority claim is contacted, but the underlying semantic evidence and counterfactual treatment remain materially compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The denial of realist linguistic priority is clear and stable, while the relevant dimensions of 'ordinary moral language' remain implicitly rather than expressly delimited.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical denial of any realist priority is stronger than the excerpt's brief appeal to unspecified linguistic work can support.

charity.alternative: The realist claim may be comparative and defeasible: counterfactual usage fits realism better even if anti-realist semantics is possible.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush denies priority but does not present the subjectivist analysis needed to compare fit with the cited counterfactual usage.

logicalCoherence.rationale: A viable subjectivist analysis could defeat realist priority, but the conditional bridge from its asserted availability to equal or better fit remains underexplained.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move appeals generally to linguists and philosophers without presenting their analysis, usage data, or treatment of the crucial counterfactual sentence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary moral-language-practice bridge by denying that ordinary usage privileges realist semantics.

representationalCharity.rationale: The rival conclusion is engaged directly, but its strongest comparative rather than exclusivist form is underdeveloped.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt expressly rejects linguistic priority for realism and says subjectivist analysis can account for ordinary moral language.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: The epistemic challenge to localized realist belief concerns its shared causal history and potentially unreliable philosophical methods, not a simple appeal to majority opinion.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker explicitly distinguishes a causal, second-order argument from raw numbers and criticizes the methods of contemporary analytic philosophers.

components.text: Whether a shared causal and methodological history can undermine confidence in localized realist belief without inferring fact-dependence from mere variation.
Whether initial plausibility remains justified after evidence that shared philosophical methods may be unreliable.

response.rationale: Bush shifts from population numbers to shared training, methods, and causal history, thereby contacting Enoch's demand for a genuine genealogy, but the move only raises the reliability question rather than demonstrating error production.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive causal-methodological demand, yet supplies a research question and analogy more than a completed debunking explanation.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move clearly distinguishes raw numbers from common causal history and potentially unreliable methods, with appropriately localized scope.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim is framed as a question about why a subset shares views and as a potential methodological explanation, fitting the limited evidence offered.

charity.alternative: Shared training can transmit reliable expertise, so common causal history is not inherently debunking.
charity.decisiveQualification: Bush's quantum-mechanics comparison acknowledges that the epistemic status depends on why the methods generate the belief.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction from head counting is sound, but common training supports debunking only with the additional premise that the methods are unreliable.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move identifies a plausible investigation and analogy but supplies little evidence that analytic philosophical methods actually cause realist error.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary genealogical-challenge bridge by identifying shared methodology as a possible causal mechanism.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response fairly leaves open reliable shared methods and focuses on the need to assess their causal and epistemic quality.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt points to common training and methods among a localized group and asks why those methods produce their shared realist views.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: A shared psychological error could causally explain realist belief even if most other people have no metaethical view, with raw population numbers serving only as a heuristic clue.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker corrects Enoch's description of Bush's argument and develops Bush's hallucination-and-drug analogy in first-person terms.

components.text: Whether a causal explanation of a localized group's mistaken realist belief can be provided without relying on cultural variation or majority disbelief.
Whether a shared psychological cause could defeat the initial justification of realist appearances.

response.rationale: Bush directly clarifies that neutral outsiders need no contrary metaethical belief and that the relevant work is done by a common error cause, not numbers; however, the actual cause remains hypothetical.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive genealogy requirement and corrects the numbers objection, but does not establish that the posited common cause exists.

precisionFindings.rationale: The roles of neutral outsiders, the localized mistaken group, raw numbers, heuristic evidence, and causal explanation are clearly distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move claims that a shared psychological error could explain the belief and treats prevalence only as heuristic, matching its hypothetical support.

charity.alternative: A debunking explanation requires evidence of an actual error-producing cause, not merely a possible common cause among believers.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
moves.proposition: Although standard evolutionary and peer-disagreement objections are unpersuasive, realism remains explanatorily superfluous and less parsimonious because moral phenomena do not require its posit.

moves.proposition: A pragmatist framework can explain moral behavior, language, and psychology descriptively and dissolve realism by rejecting the shared problem-setting assumptions of standard metaethics.
